req.title: Register requires username
req.statement: The system shall render the register form with an error message when POST /auth/register omits the username.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /auth/register must render the register form with 'Username is required.' when username is omitted. We need: (1) a positive case confirming valid registration works (no error), (2) a negative case confirming missing username yields the exact error message with HTTP 200, (3) a boundary case confirming empty-string username (the exact boundary between absent and present) also triggers the error. Additional cases cover the decision table (password missing vs username missing) and state transition (form re-rendered, not redirected). All assertions use exact values to kill constant/operator mutations.

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'password': 'secret'})
assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200, got {r.status_code}'
assert b'Username is required.' in r.data, 'Error message not found in response'

        init_db()

    assert b'Username is required.' in resp.data
